title: Establish latency envelopes, progressive error budgets, and deployment gates for inference routes
creator: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary:
Define a clear set of SLOs expressed as latency envelopes (P50/P95/P99 targets), progressive error-budget consumption rules, and a decision matrix that gates staged rollouts for different inference route classes (interactive chat, completion, embeddings, high-throughput batch). This ticket collects requirements, defines acceptance criteria, and lays out the rollout gating matrix and automatic degradation actions (throttling, model fallback, reduced max tokens).

Background & motivation:
Current host API rollouts have relied on heuristic thresholds and ad-hoc runbooks. As traffic diversity grows (low-latency chat vs bulk embeddings) we need deterministic service contracts that product and platform teams can rely on. These contracts must: (1) set observable latency envelopes per route class, (2) specify how error budgets are computed and consumed over rolling windows, and (3) define automated gating and graceful degradation actions when budgets approach exhaustion.

Goals & success metrics:
- Establish P50/P95/P99 latency targets per route class and region where applicable.
- Define error budget windows (1h, 24h, 7d) and consumption rules.
- Create a gating matrix that maps observed signal -> action (canary pause, rollback, autoscale trigger, model fallback, token-length caps).
- Automate a minimal set of degradation actions (throttling, fallback) via console policies and runtime hooks.
- Acceptance: run a staged rollout with simulated traffic that exercises each gate and demonstrates expected behavior in >= 3 regions with no user-visible correctness regressions.

Scope (in):
- Define SLOs for: hosted API chat, hosted API completions, embeddings, and server-side batch endpoints.
- Define error budget math and visualization requirements for Console.
- Outline automated actions and the minimal runtime hooks required (throttle rate, fallback model mapping, token caps).
- Produce the gating matrix and PRD for Console UI controls (canary window, thresholds, auto-rollback toggle).

Out of scope:
- Dedicated-only SLO contract design (separate PM ticket).
- Full implementation of autoscaling algorithms (engine team to own).
- Long-term archival reporting beyond 90 days.

Measurement methodology:
- Latency envelopes measured at request-end for user-perceived end-to-end time (client request -> first-byte and final-byte). We will publish P50/P95/P99 samples sampled at 100% for 1 minute and aggregated for windows.
- Error = responses with HTTP 5xx or runtime-produced model-fallback errors flagged as degraded.
- Error budget = allocated allowable percent of errors per window (e.g., 0.1% per 24h for P95 target failure). Specific budgets described in acceptance criteria.

Rollout gating matrix (summary):
- Green: metrics within envelope -> proceed with canary expansion.
- Yellow: P95 breaches < 10% above envelope OR error budget consumption between 30%-70% -> pause expansion; enable conservative autoscaling and increased sampling for traces; notify PM/Oncall.
- Orange: P95 breaches 10%-30% above OR error budget 70%-90% -> trigger automated mitigation: reduce max tokens by 25%, enable model fallback to cheaper compatible variant, enable temporary per-key rate limit at 80% baseline. Pause rollout and require manual approval to proceed.
- Red: P95 breach >30% above OR error budget >90% or sustained 5xx spike -> rollback to previous version, roll back route weight to pre-canary baseline, open incident and create postmortem.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
1) A PRD describing per-route SLO numbers: example candidates -> Chat: P50<=60ms, P95<=250ms, P99<=600ms; Completions: P50<=40ms, P95<=200ms, P99<=500ms; Embeddings: P50<=20ms, P95<=100ms, P99<=300ms. These numbers are placeholders and must be validated in performance benchmarking.
2) Error budgets defined: Chat: 0.3%/24h; Completions: 0.2%/24h; Embeddings: 0.1%/24h. Windows for consumption: 1h rolling, 24h, 7d.
3) A gating matrix with concrete automated actions implemented as Console policy configs (can be toggled).
4) End-to-end test harness that replays synthetic traffic patterns to validate gate transitions and mitigation actions.
5) Dashboard mockups and alert definitions (PagerDuty runbook link) attached to PRD.
6) Run a staged canary in one region with 5%, 20%, 50% ramps proving gate behavior; stash results as artifacts.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Alert A: P95 breach sustained for 5 minutes -> severity S2, notify oncall, create temporary pause on canary.
- Alert B: Error budget consumption >70% (24h window) -> notify SRE + PM.
- Alert C: Automatic rollback executed -> page SRE and product oncall and attach rollback details to ticket.

Trade-offs & open decisions:
- Tolerance levels: initial latency targets are deliberately conservative to prioritize reliability; may tighten after perf work.
- Automated rollback vs. manual intervention: we favor automated rollback on severe signals to protect customers, but will expose a kill-switch in Console to disable auto-rollback for enterprise customers with negotiated SLAs.
- Measurement overhead: full sampling of P99 increases cost; proposal uses adaptive sampling where sustained near-threshold signals cause increased trace sampling.

Links & artifacts:
- Benchmark plan (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/slo-bench-plan (placeholder)
- Console mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/slo-console-mockups
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/slo-rollout-runbook
- Measurement PR (ENG): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4832

Implementation notes for Eng & Console teams:
- Eng to instrument latency histograms and expose streaming metrics for error-budget windows.
- Console to add widgets for error budget burn (1h/24h/7d) and gating control UI (enable/disable, threshold override).
- Product to own canary sequence and rollout policy defaults; work with solutions engineering for enterprise overrides.

Next steps / milestones:
- Mar 12: Finalize PRD and SLO candidates (this ticket).
- Mar 15: Engineering spike to validate current P95/P99 under representative load (estimate 3 days).
- Mar 22: Console UI prototype for gating controls.
- Mar 26-30: Run canary in us-west-2 with synthetic traffic and real user shadowing.

Comments & review log:
- 2026-03-10 Aisha K: Created ticket and initial draft.
- 2026-03-11 Liam O'C: Updated latency candidates after quick perf run; suggested lowering chat P95 to 220ms based on us-west data.
- 2026-03-12 Priya Gupta (Eng): Reviewed gating actions; requested explicit mapping of fallback model names and API compatibility checks.
- 2026-03-12 Security team: flagged fallback model selection for data-leak review (action: security_review_required=false for now; escalate if private deployments requested).

Owner notes / decisions to record:
- Use adaptive trace sampling to reduce cost while preserving signal fidelity.
- Enterprise customers will get an opt-out for auto-rollback as a configuration flag in Console.

If approved, this PRD should be broken into two engineering epics: (1) metrics + runtime mitigation hooks, (2) Console gating UI + rollout orchestration.
